## The short version

**You do not need to install anything, and you do not need to run any code.**

This session is a guided walkthrough. {{< var session.presenter >}} will write and run
the code live on screen. Everything he types is already written out, with its output,
in the [walkthrough]({{< var site.url >}}notebook.html) — so you can read along on a
second window, or just watch and come back to it afterward.

Running the code yourself during the session is **optional**. If you want to, the setup
is below. If it doesn't work on the day, let it go and follow along; nothing in the
session depends on your machine.


## What you'll get

| | |
|---|---|
| Walkthrough (read-along, all outputs shown) | [{{< var site.url >}}notebook.html]({{< var site.url >}}notebook.html) |
| Everything as a single download | [workshop-materials.zip]({{< var site.zip >}}) |
| Source and version history | [{{< var site.repo >}}]({{< var site.repo >}}) |
| Archived + citable | {{< var site.doi >}} |

The ZIP contains the synthetic dataset and its codebook, the crosswalk file (the lookup
table that turns ZIP codes into Census ZCTAs), the walkthrough source with its Stata and
Python equivalents, and an offline copy of this site.

**The NaNDA files themselves are not in the ZIP.** NaNDA is distributed through ICPSR,
which asks for a free account, so we can't pass the files along for you — you download
your own, which takes about five minutes. The steps are in the optional setup below and
in `data/nanda/README.md` inside the ZIP. You only need them if you want to run the
code; every output is already on the [walkthrough]({{< var site.url >}}notebook.html).

## If you do want to run along

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Optional setup (about 10 minutes, do it before the day)

1. **R** (4.3 or newer) — <https://cran.r-project.org/>
2. **RStudio Desktop** (free) — <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>
3. Open RStudio and run:

   ```r
   install.packages(c("tidyverse", "here", "janitor"))
   ```

   (`readxl`, which reads the crosswalk, installs as part of `tidyverse`.)

4. Download and unzip [workshop-materials.zip]({{< var site.zip >}}).
5. **Get the NaNDA files from ICPSR.** Sign in at <https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/> with a
   free account, then download these in **R** format (Stata and delimited versions are
   on the same pages):

   - **{{< var nanda.social_services_name >}}** — the ZCTA 2010 file.
     <{{< var nanda.social_services_doi >}}>
   - **{{< var nanda.parks_name >}}** — dataset 2 (DS0002).
     <{{< var nanda.parks_doi >}}>
   - **NaNDA: Socioeconomic Status** — datasets 3 and 8 (DS0003 and DS0008).
     <https://doi.org/10.3886/ICPSR38528>

   Unzip each one, dig the data file out of the nested folders, and put all four in
   `data/nanda/` inside the unzipped workshop folder. `data/nanda/README.md` has the
   filenames and the same steps in more detail.

6. Open `workshop.Rproj`, then open `notebook.qmd`, and run the first chunk. If it
   prints a preview of the data, you're set.

**Stata and Python users:** equivalent `.do` files are in the `stata/` folder of the
ZIP and `.py` scripts in `python/`. The live session is in R, but these do the same
thing step for step and are yours to keep.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## If setup doesn't work

Save the troubleshooting for later. The walkthrough page has every output already
rendered, so nothing you'd see by running the code is missing from it. Follow along on
screen, and email us afterward: **nanda-admin@umich.edu**.
:::

## What we assume you already know

You've used R, Stata, or another statistical package to open a dataset and join two
tables. This is **not** an R lesson. It's about what goes wrong when you link
individual-level data to neighborhood-level data, and how to catch it, in whichever
language you use.

## What's out of scope

Geocoding street addresses to census tracts. The synthetic dataset includes addresses,
and we'll point at how you'd do it, but it isn't part of this session.
